meta.title: Motomation Design
meta.description: Use when designing, building, redesigning, animating, or critiquing any website, landing page, portfolio, storefront, or web UI where the result must look original and award-level instead of AI-templated. The design direction is derived from the brief; the skill is a generator, not a style library.
meta.job: every site you make must look like it was designed for this brief by a person with taste, never like it came out of a template.

author.name: Asfakul Islam
author.bio: Building Tomorrows Web Today with MERN Magic!

laws.title: Think before you draw.
laws.text: Run the Thinking Sequence before writing any UI code. No exceptions for "simple" pages.

laws.title: Type is chosen first, in one of two modes.
laws.text: Pick the mode from the brief, write it in the plan with the reason, and design fully inside it. Neither mode is a fallback for the other.

laws.title: Motion must mean something.
laws.text: Every animation answers "what does this tell the user?" If the answer is "nothing", delete it.

laws.title: Actively reduce repetition.
laws.text: Draw constraints from `scripts/collide.mjs` (no archetype or signature repeats inside a run) and compare your plan's structural choices (archetype, signature, type, palette, tier) against `.motomation/log.json` with `scripts/memory.mjs check`. This detects and reduces repetition inside one project; it cannot guarantee novelty across projects that don't share a log, so say so when it matters.

laws.title: Ship complete, accessible, fast.
laws.text: No placeholders, no lorem ipsum, no broken reduced-motion, no fake numbers.

steps.name: Stack
steps.body: Before any design step, know what you are building in. The stack changes what the design can be (server rendering, islands, a single file, a build step), so it is decided first and never guessed.

steps.name: Tension
steps.body: Every good brief hides a conflict. Design lives in that conflict.

steps.name: Concept
steps.body: The concept resolves the tension in one sentence. It is an idea, not a layout or a colour.

steps.name: Archetype + Mutation
steps.body: Derive the page's structure from the concept. `structures/archetypes.md` and `data/archetypes.csv` are reference and constraint: they tell you what structures exist and what each one demands, not which one to take. Then **mutate** it: break one rule of that structure on purpose.

steps.name: Forced Collision
steps.body: Take something from a world unrelated to the brief and steal **one property** from it. This is where original patterns come from.

steps.name: Signature Move
steps.body: Invent one interaction or motion that people will remember and describe. Use `signatures/` for inspiration, then make it specific to this concept.

steps.name: Anti-Sameness Check
steps.body: Compare your plan against three things: 1. **The AI-default list** in `gates/delivery-gate.md`. Count the matches. 2. **Project memory (IDs and structure):** run    `node scripts/memory.mjs check --archetype <x> --signature <y> --tier <n> --sections hero,work,contact --type-scale <ratio>`.    It checks two things against the last 5 runs. First, exact IDs: an archetype or signature already used. Second, a **structural fingerprint**: layout family, type-scale bucket, section order, motion tier and signature type, scored 0–100%. A different archetype with the same rows layout, the same section order and the same kind of signature is still a repeat. At **≥ 70%** the script names the run you're rebuilding and the dimensions that match, and offers a mutation aimed at the heaviest one. Apply it (or justify the overlap in one line) and check again. Exit code 2 means a clash. `/invent` prints each draw's partial fingerprint and flags draws that rebuild a recent page. After delivery, `memory.mjs log` with the same flags stores the fingerprint. Without a shell, compare the five dimensions by hand against `.motomation/log.json`. 3. **The obvious version:** write down what a template would do. Your plan must differ in at least **three** of: structure, type, colour, motion, signature, imagery.

commands.what: turns a section into a Tier 5 scroll-film: storyboard in `MOTION.md`, technique choice (DOM, image sequence, video, WebGL), asset pipeline, code and fallbacks.
commands.when: a product, place or story should play like a film as you scroll.

commands.what: adds motion to existing UI at the given tier, following the four questions.
commands.when: the design is done but static.
commands.output: a motion plan (what moves, why, tokens) + code.

commands.what: a typography pass: face choice with reasons, fluid scale, tracking, wrapping, numerals, variable-axis opportunities.
commands.when: the page feels generic, and the type is usually why.

commands.what: Raises ENERGY by one step: bigger type jumps, stronger contrast, a braver accent moment, one more grid break. Keeps the concept.
Lowers ENERGY and/or MOTION by one step: more air, fewer moving parts, softer accent, slower reveals.
Removes until only the essential remains. Runs the Restraint Gate hard: one signature, one accent, fewer sections.
Keeps the content and concept but changes the **structure**: a different archetype or mutation, drawn with `collide.mjs`. Use it when the layout feels like a template.
A generate → critique → improve loop, up to 3 rounds. Each round scores the six critique axes and fixes the lowest one. Stops when every axis is 4 or more. Use it for flagship pages.
A design review in the format of `commands/critique-format.md`: scores, the three most important problems, and fixes in priority order. Doesn't change code unless asked.
A technical gate: accessibility, performance, reduced motion, mobile matrix, SEO and the AI-default scan. Returns pass/fail per item with file and line references.

Extracts the **design DNA** of a reference **without copying it**, and writes it into `DESIGN.md` as a "Studied direction" in five sections: type, palette, layout, motion, signature. It ends with what to take (decisions) and what to leave (anything that would make a copy). Agent-driven: the agent opens the URL or reads the screenshot, and no script fetches anything. Measured values are marked as measured, and missing evidence as `not observed`. Full input, output and rules: `commands/study.md`.

The final pass: spacing rhythm, alignment, typographic details (quotes, dashes, numerals), focus states, hover/press states, empty and error states, loading, favicon and OG image, the stamp comment and the memory log.

scan.q: Is the page hero → logo wall → 3 features → testimonials → pricing → CTA?
Is the hero a centred headline + subtitle + two buttons + a screenshot, without a reason?
Is there a bento grid without a concept reason?
Do all sections use the same layout?
Is the nav "logo left, 5 links centre, button right", and the footer four columns of links, without thought?
Is the display font Inter, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Poppins, Montserrat, Arial, Helvetica or the system UI stack? Is Playfair Display and Space Grotesk used without a stated reason?
Is there a purple/blue/pink gradient, a glowing orb or blurred blobs without meaning?
Is glassmorphism used without the concept needing layers?
Is there an icon above every feature title?
Are there more than one accent colour or more than one display face, without a reason?
Is every corner the same large radius, with a shadow and a border all at once?
Is the hero image a generic stock photo or AI art with no relation to the brief?
Is there lorem ipsum, "Acme", "John Doe", or placeholder copy?
Are there invented statistics, logos, testimonials or awards?
Does the copy contain any banned phrase from `craft/copy.md`?
Are there emoji used as icons or bullets?
Does anything fade-up on scroll just because it can?
Is any animation missing a reduced-motion path?
Are layout properties animated?
Do UI feedback animations exceed 250ms, or use ease-in or `scale(0)` entrances?
Is the scroll hijacked (custom scroll that breaks keyboard, anchor links or screen readers)?
Does any loop or canvas keep running off-screen?
Are there TODOs, `// ...rest`, or unfinished components?
Are there clickable `div`s, missing labels or missing `alt` text?
Are there `markers: true`, console logs or unused imports left in?
Does more than one section headline share the same shape (all questions, all "X. Y." fragments, all mirror sentences)?
Does any sentence end in a vague "-ing" benefit tail, or cite unnamed experts or studies?
Is the same thing called by more than one name across the page (synonym cycling)?
Does an em dash appear in most paragraphs, or does every section close with a generic invitation?

gateChecks.name: Contrast
gateChecks.fails: below 4.5:1 for body text, below 3:1 for large text (≥ 24px, or ≥ 18.66px bold)

gateChecks.name: Overflow
gateChecks.fails: the page scrolls sideways, or an element leaves the viewport or pushes text out of its parent by more than 1px with no clipping ancestor

gateChecks.name: Long display words
gateChecks.fails: the text is wider than its box, leaves the viewport, breaks a word across lines, or splits one word across elements (e.g. "Have" + "li" on two door leaves)

gateChecks.name: Reduced motion
gateChecks.fails: text that is visible normally is hidden, or pixels keep changing on a still page

gateChecks.name: Alt and names
gateChecks.fails: an `img` has no `alt`, or a link, button, input or other focusable element has no accessible name

gateChecks.name: Numbers
gateChecks.fails: an element is visible with a value that is later corrected: "0 hectares" before a count-up runs, a price replaced after load, a counter that never runs under reduced motion

gateChecks.name: Motion quality
gateChecks.fails: a zone whose median change between samples is ≤ 0.5% of pixels (pinned but static) · p95 over 20 ms at 1440 or over 25 ms at 375 ×4, **judged only on an unconstrained machine**: in a sandbox it prints `not verified — san

gateChecks.name: Accessibility
gateChecks.fails: focus changes < 1% of the pixels around the element (no visible ring) · a target under 24×24px (WCAG 2.5.8; inline links in a sentence exempt; under 44px is a warning, not counted) · text clipped by an `overflow: hidden`

gateChecks.name: The four rule sets
gateChecks.fails: any rule in the set fails; warnings (unsourced claims, long paragraphs, missing JSON-LD, unstated og:image size, unminified scripts, dev builds) are printed and not counted

components.name: Blur Focus
components.what: Words sharpen from a soft blur into focus, one after another, as the line enters the screen.
components.use_when: The concept is about clarity, focus, eyesight, photography or waking up.
components.avoid_when: Every heading on the page; long paragraphs; low-end devices with many instances.
components.reduced_motion: Text is sharp and visible from the start.
components.a11y: Plain text in the DOM; only filter and opacity animate.

components.name: Curved Text
components.what: Text set around a circle like a stamp or seal, with an optional slow turn.
components.use_when: Badges, stamps, seals, "since" marks and a single rotating label beside a primary action.
components.avoid_when: Anything the reader must read quickly; as a loading spinner; more than one per screen.
components.reduced_motion: The ring is still.
components.a11y: The SVG has role img and the text as its label.

components.name: Decode
components.what: A short label resolves from random glyphs, left to right, when it enters the screen or on hover.
components.use_when: Technical, secret or data-led brands; labels of 1–4 words.
components.avoid_when: Body text, headlines longer than a line, or more than one per screen.
components.reduced_motion: Shows the final text at once; no glyph cycling.
components.touch: Runs on enter; hover replay is mouse-only.
components.a11y: The real text is the accessible name; the cycling glyphs are aria-hidden.

components.name: Ink Fill
components.what: A statement starts in the muted colour and fills with ink word by word as the reader scrolls through it.
components.use_when: Manifestos, about statements, a single paragraph that is the page's idea.
components.avoid_when: More than one per page; text the reader needs before scrolling (it must stay readable when muted).
components.reduced_motion: The whole statement is in ink from the start.
components.a11y: Plain text; only colour changes, and the muted colour must still pass 4.5:1 for body text or 3:1 for large text.

components.name: Letter Relay
components.what: A large hero name shrinks and travels into a fixed header slot letter by letter as you scroll the first screen, so the name hands itself to the navigation.
components.use_when: Portfolios and personal brands where the name is the identity.
components.avoid_when: Long names (over ~16 characters); pages without a fixed header; product pages.
components.reduced_motion: The hero name and the header name are both static; no scroll listener runs.
components.a11y: The h1 keeps the real text; the travelling letters are aria-hidden; the header name is a normal link.

components.name: Neighbour Moves
components.what: Each letter of a name has its own small move on hover (lift, tilt, stretch, spin, drop), so the word feels like a cast of characters.
components.use_when: Personal names, studio names and light-hearted logotypes of 3–12 letters.
components.avoid_when: Navigation, body text, or brands that must feel calm.
components.reduced_motion: No hover moves.
components.touch: A tap on a letter plays its move once.
components.a11y: The word is the accessible name; letters are aria-hidden.

components.name: Pressure Type
components.what: Each letter of one display word stretches wider and heavier as the cursor nears it, like pressing into rubber.
components.use_when: Playful, elastic or physical brands with a variable font that has wdth and wght axes.
components.avoid_when: Fonts without variable axes; more than one word; any body copy.
components.reduced_motion: Letters stay at the base width and weight.
components.a11y: The word is the accessible name; letter spans are aria-hidden.

components.name: Scroll Float
components.what: Letters of a display line rise and settle into place one by one, driven by scroll position, so scrolling back reverses it.
components.use_when: Light-hearted display lines that should feel buoyant; one line per section.
components.avoid_when: Serious or institutional briefs; text that must be readable before it settles (prices, dates).
components.reduced_motion: Letters sit in place; no scroll listener runs.
components.a11y: The line is the accessible name; letter spans are aria-hidden.

components.name: Split Flap
components.what: Each character flips through the alphabet to its value like a departure board, settling left to right; changing the value flips again.
components.use_when: Schedules, line-ups, menus, travel, times and short codes.
components.avoid_when: Long text; values the reader must trust mid-animation (the final value is announced, not the flips).
components.reduced_motion: Shows the new value at once.
components.a11y: aria-live announces the final value only; flipping glyphs are aria-hidden.

components.name: Width Sprint
components.what: A display word stretches wider the faster you scroll and relaxes back when you stop, using the font's width axis.
components.use_when: Sport, speed, events and launches with a variable font that has a wdth axis.
components.avoid_when: Fonts without wdth; more than one element; layouts where the word could overflow at its widest.
components.reduced_motion: The word stays at its base width.
components.a11y: Plain text; only font-variation-settings changes.

components.name: ASCII Text
components.what: A word drawn as a grid of characters, sampled from the word's own letterforms; it settles out of character noise when it enters the screen.
components.use_when: The concept is code, print terminals, telegrams, early computing or textile grids; one short word at display size.
components.avoid_when: Anything longer than about 12 characters; small sizes (it becomes noise); as the only copy of important text.
components.reduced_motion: The finished character drawing, with no noise.
components.touch: Same as desktop (settles when in view).
components.a11y: The element has the word as its accessible name (role="img" + aria-label); the character grid is aria-hidden. The grid is sized from its container width, so it never overflows.

components.name: Glitch
components.what: On hover, focus or tap, the word tears for a moment: two offset colour copies slip sideways in thin bands, then it settles. Never loops.
components.use_when: The concept is a broken signal, a corrupted file, a jump cut or an error that matters; one word or a short label.
components.avoid_when: Body text; anything that must be read during the effect; brands that want calm; more than one per page.
components.reduced_motion: Plain text; nothing tears.
components.touch: Tap plays the tear once (no hover needed). Focus on anything inside it (a link it wraps) plays it too.
components.a11y: The word is plain text; the colour copies are aria-hidden. One burst lasts 320ms and can't repeat more than once a second, so it never flashes three times in a second (WCAG 2.3.1). Bands move with transform and clip-path on the copies only.

components.name: Rotating Words
components.what: One word in a sentence turns over to the next, like a rolling counter, a few times, then rests. The slot is as wide as the longest word (with the sentence's ending attached), so nothing around it moves.
components.use_when: The sentence really has several true endings (who you serve, what you make), and the rest of the line stays still.
components.avoid_when: More than one per page; endings that are adjectives about yourself ("innovative", "bold"); the hero's only message.
components.reduced_motion: The first word, still; all the words are listed for assistive tech.
components.touch: Same as desktop; it pauses while touched.
components.a11y: Screen readers get every word once, as a plain list in the sentence; the turning slot is aria-hidden. It stops by itself after `cycles` rounds (default 2), pauses on hover and focus, and pauses off screen (WCAG 2.2.2).

components.name: Scramble on Hover
components.what: Letters near the pointer scramble into other glyphs, like a magnet passing over iron filings, and settle back as it moves on. Unlike Decode, it reacts locally, where the cursor is.
components.use_when: A short label the visitor plays with (a name, a nav word, a project title) on a code, cipher or signal concept.
components.avoid_when: Words the visitor must read while pointing at them (buttons with actions); long text; for a one-time reveal (use Decode).
components.reduced_motion: Plain text; nothing scrambles.
components.touch: Tap scrambles the whole word once, settling left to right.
components.a11y: The word is plain text for assistive tech (the scrambled letters are an aria-hidden copy). At rest the word is set in its own glyph widths; while it scrambles each letter is held at the width its real glyph measured, so the word never reflows. Keyboard focus plays the tap version.

components.name: Shiny Text
components.what: A single band of light passes once across a short label, like light catching foil or a brass plate, when it enters the screen and again on hover.
components.use_when: The material is metal, foil, glass or a printed seal; one short label or badge.
components.avoid_when: Large headlines (the moving gradient is paint-heavy: cost grows with area); body text; infinite loops; as a "premium" sticker on everything.
components.reduced_motion: Solid ink, no light band.
components.touch: Plays once when in view; tap replays it.
components.a11y: Plain text. The ink colour is the base everywhere and the band only lightens it, so pick a `shine` that still contrasts with the ground. Solid ink at rest; the clipped gradient is added only while the band crosses (and never where background-clip: text isn't supported). Paint-heavy (moving gradient), so it runs once per trigger, never in a loop (motion/tokens.md "What to animate").

components.name: Typewriter
components.what: A line types itself out, character by character, when it scrolls into view, with a caret that fades once the line is complete.
components.use_when: The concept is a terminal, a typed letter, a dispatch or a confession; one line, read once.
components.avoid_when: Headlines the visitor needs at once; more than one per screen; long paragraphs; anything repeated on every visit.
components.reduced_motion: The whole line is there from the start, with no caret.
components.touch: Same as desktop (starts when in view).
components.a11y: The full text is in the DOM for assistive tech from the first render; the typed copy is aria-hidden. Every character holds its final place, so the line never reflows (no layout shift).

components.name: Aperture
components.what: The next section opens through a growing circle (an iris) as you scroll into it, from a small porthole to full bleed.
components.use_when: A chapter change that is a real threshold: entering a room, a lens, a window, a reveal of the product.
components.avoid_when: Every section; content that must be readable at the edges before the iris opens.
components.reduced_motion: The section is fully open from the start.
components.a11y: Content is always in the DOM and readable by assistive tech; only clip-path animates.

components.name: Darkroom Develop
components.what: A photograph develops from blank paper as it scrolls in: pale and flat first, then contrast, then tone, like a print in the tray.
components.use_when: Photography, archives, memory, analogue brands; one image per screen.
components.avoid_when: Product shots the buyer must inspect; galleries of many small images.
components.reduced_motion: The photo is fully developed from the start.
components.a11y: A normal img with alt; only CSS filters change.

components.name: Horizontal Reel
components.what: A section pins and vertical scroll pulls a strip of frames sideways, like film through a gate; a frame counter follows.
components.use_when: Film, gallery, timeline and process concepts with 4–10 frames.
components.avoid_when: Content people need to scan quickly; more than one per page; frames that need reading time.
components.reduced_motion: The frames become a normal horizontally scrollable row with snap points.
components.touch: Below 768px wide, or under 560px tall (200% zoom), the strip becomes a swipeable row with snap points (no pinning).
components.a11y: A normal list; the counter is aria-hidden; every frame is reachable by keyboard in the fallback.

components.name: Reading Rail
components.what: A thin rail at the top or edge of the screen fills as you read an article, with an optional chapter label that changes at each heading.
components.use_when: Long reads, case studies and documentation pages.
components.avoid_when: Short pages; landing pages; next to another progress indicator.
components.reduced_motion: The rail still reflects progress (it's information, not decoration) but moves in 5% steps instead of continuously.
components.a11y: role progressbar with aria-valuenow, updated at most every 5%.

components.name: Stacked Deck
components.what: Cards stick one after another and stack like a deck; covered cards step back and dim, leaving their titles as a table of contents.
components.use_when: Sequences, case studies, steps and services with 3–6 items.
components.avoid_when: More than 6 cards; cards taller than the viewport; content that must be compared side by side.
components.reduced_motion: A plain ordered list in normal flow: no sticky, no scale, no dim; every card is a full, readable block.
components.touch: Same as desktop; on short screens the offset per card shrinks.
components.a11y: A normal ordered list; every card is reachable and readable.

components.name: Thread
components.what: One line draws itself down the page as you scroll, linking sections like a seam, a route or a timeline.
components.use_when: Journeys, timelines, craft (stitching, drawing), routes and process pages.
components.avoid_when: As decoration on a page without a journey; together with another scroll signature.
components.reduced_motion: The line is fully drawn and still.
components.a11y: The SVG is decorative (aria-hidden); the content sits above it in normal flow.

components.name: Velocity Marquee
components.what: A looping marquee that drifts on its own, speeds up with scroll speed, follows scroll direction and leans (skews) while you scroll fast.
components.use_when: Sport, launches, events and a single line of brand words between sections.
components.avoid_when: Content the reader needs (prices, dates); more than one marquee per page.
components.reduced_motion: A static, wrapped row of the same words.
components.a11y: The words are read once (the duplicated copies are aria-hidden); hovering or focusing pauses the drift.

components.name: Image Trail
components.what: Moving the cursor across an area drops a trail of images that appear, linger briefly and shrink away, cycling through a set.
components.use_when: Photographers, archives, studios with a deep body of work; one area per page.
components.avoid_when: Fewer than 5 images; e-commerce product pages; over text that must be read.
components.reduced_motion: The images are shown as a static row instead.
components.a11y: Trail images are decorative (empty alt) because the static row, with alt text, is always in the DOM for assistive tech.

components.name: Lens
components.what: A circle follows the cursor and reveals a second layer underneath: sketch under final, night under day, before under after.
components.use_when: The two layers are the story (process, transformation, hidden detail).
components.avoid_when: The second layer is decoration; text-heavy layers; more than one per page.
components.reduced_motion: The lens jumps to the cursor without easing; a "Show the other layer" toggle shows the second layer at full size.
components.touch: Press and drag to move the lens; the toggle works everywhere.
components.a11y: Both layers are in the DOM; the toggle is a real button with aria-pressed; give images alt text.

components.name: Pixel Wake
components.what: The cursor leaves a trail of square pixels on a grid that fade out behind it, like a wake on a low-resolution screen.
components.use_when: Digital, pixel, retro, game and screen-themed concepts; usually only over the hero.
components.avoid_when: Over body text; on calm or luxury briefs; together with another cursor effect.
components.reduced_motion: No trail.
components.a11y: A decorative canvas (aria-hidden) that never blocks clicks (pointer-events none).

components.name: Seismograph Line
components.what: A hairline divider bends toward the cursor as it passes and springs back with a small wobble, like a needle on a seismograph.
components.use_when: Dividers on calm editorial pages where one living detail is enough; sound, measurement and science brands.
components.avoid_when: Every divider; busy pages; pages that already have a cursor effect.
components.reduced_motion: A straight line.
components.a11y: Decorative: role presentation, aria-hidden.

components.name: Target Cursor
components.what: A small crosshair follows the cursor; over anything clickable it snaps out into corner brackets that frame the target.
components.use_when: Precision tools, cameras, games, architecture and engineering concepts.
components.avoid_when: Content sites; together with another cursor effect; when it would hide the system cursor (it doesn't by default).
components.reduced_motion: Brackets jump to targets without easing.
components.a11y: Decorative overlay (aria-hidden, pointer-events none); the system cursor stays visible unless hideCursor is set.

components.name: Tilt Card
components.what: A card rotates in 3D toward the cursor with a soft moving highlight, like holding a physical card to the light.
components.use_when: Physical objects: tickets, cards, passes, packaging, a single product.
components.avoid_when: Grids of many cards; text-heavy cards; cards that are links to long content (the motion distracts).
components.reduced_motion: Flat card, no rotation or highlight.
components.a11y: Children render normally; the highlight is aria-hidden.

components.name: Aurora
components.what: Curtains of northern light hang across a night sky: a sharp lower hem, fading upward in vertical rays, folding slowly. A small WebGL shader draws it; a CSS poster stands in everywhere else.
components.use_when: The subject is the far north, night, cold, observation, polar travel or a planetarium: behind a hero or a single quiet section.
components.avoid_when: As a generic "AI glow" background; behind body copy; light themes; pages that already run WebGL.
components.reduced_motion: A designed still, not a frozen frame: a long-exposure plate. The curtains settle into three smooth ribbons of the same two colours over a dark ridge, under circular star trails; no canvas is mounted.
components.touch: Renders at two-thirds resolution on coarse pointers.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). Capability probe first (Save-Data, ≤ 2 cores, < 4 GB, no or software WebGL → poster only); DPR ≤ 1.5; paused off screen and in hidden tabs; poster and canvas fill the same absolute box, so no layout shift. Keep `sky` dark: text on top is checked against the sky, and the curtains stay in the upper half.

components.name: Beams
components.what: Parallel shafts of sunlight fall through a row of high windows (a clerestory, a mill, a stage rig) at one shared angle and sway slightly in depth. CSS 3D only: soft gradient shafts rotated in a perspective space; no WebGL, because transforms are enough here.
components.use_when: Churches, mills, warehouses, galleries, theatres, anything lit through high windows: behind one dark hero.
components.avoid_when: Bright themes; as "spotlight on our product" decoration; together with other moving backgrounds.
components.reduced_motion: A designed still: noon held. Hard-edged shafts fall through the windows and land as bright pools on the floor, dust caught in the light; not the sway stopped.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). Capability probe (Save-Data, ≤ 2 cores, < 4 GB → still poster); only transform animates (composite-only), via Web Animations that pause off screen and in hidden tabs; absolute box, so no layout shift. Shafts are faint (≤ 0.36 alpha) and their soft edges are a static mask on a transformed layer (not animated), so text contrast is checked on the ground. No canvas, so no DPR cost.

components.name: Contour Lines
components.what: Topographic contour lines drawn as SVG that slowly drift, like a map breathing; deterministic from a seed.
components.use_when: Landscape, outdoors, climate, geography, agriculture and mapping concepts.
components.avoid_when: Urban or tech brands without a land story; behind dense text.
components.reduced_motion: Still lines.
components.a11y: Decorative SVG (aria-hidden). The drift is a CSS transform on three composited layers: no JS and no repaint per frame.

components.name: Dot Field
components.what: A grid of dots that swell and push away from the cursor, then ease back, like a pin-art board.
components.use_when: Technical, structural, data or grid-led concepts; behind a hero with little text.
components.avoid_when: Behind body text; organic or luxury briefs; together with a cursor signature.
components.reduced_motion: A still dot grid.
components.a11y: Decorative canvas (aria-hidden, pointer-events none); paused off screen and in hidden tabs.

components.name: Globe
components.what: A sphere of evenly spaced dots turns slowly, the far side faint, with a few brighter markers for real places (lat/lon). WebGL points; a CSS dotted disc stands in everywhere else.
components.use_when: The business is genuinely about places on Earth (shipping, a diaspora, offices in named cities, a travel route), and the markers are real.
components.avoid_when: As a generic "global" or "scale" signal; with invented markers; on pages that already run WebGL; at small sizes (the dots turn to noise).
components.reduced_motion: A designed still: a chart plate of the globe facing the first marker, drawn in line (graticule, rim, the markers ringed and joined by arcs in order), not the dot sphere stopped. No canvas is mounted.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden): list the places in text nearby too. Capability probe (Save-Data, ≤ 2 cores, < 4 GB, no or software WebGL → poster); DPR ≤ 1.5; paused off screen and in hidden tabs; fills its absolute box, so no layout shift.

components.name: Grain
components.what: A film-grain layer over a section or the whole page, static by default or gently flickering at a low frame rate.
components.use_when: Analogue, photographic, warm or printed brands; to take the digital edge off flat colour.
components.avoid_when: Over small text at high opacity; on clinical, technical brands; animated on low-end mobile.
components.reduced_motion: Static grain.
components.touch: Static grain (flicker is skipped on coarse pointers to save battery).
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden, pointer-events none); keep opacity low enough that contrast still passes.

components.name: Halftone
components.what: Renders an image as print dots on a canvas, sized by brightness, like a newspaper photo; dots can grow in as it enters the screen.
components.use_when: Print, newspaper, zine, poster, protest and retro concepts.
components.avoid_when: Product photos people must inspect; portraits where likeness matters; many on one page.
components.reduced_motion: Dots render at full size immediately.
components.touch: The dots print at full size a few rows per frame, top to bottom, like a press: growing thousands of dots every
components.a11y: The canvas has role img and the alt text; the source image needs CORS headers if it's on another origin.

components.name: Light Sweep
components.what: A slow band of light crosses a surface every few seconds, like sun moving through a window or a scanner pass.
components.use_when: Architecture, light, time-of-day and hospitality concepts; behind one hero or one card.
components.avoid_when: Behind text where the band would drop contrast; as a "shimmer" on buttons; more than one per screen.
components.reduced_motion: No sweep.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden, pointer-events none). CSS only.

components.name: Liquid Field
components.what: Slow flowing colour like ink in water or silk in wind, drawn by a tiny WebGL fragment shader with a CSS gradient fallback.
components.use_when: The material really is liquid, fabric, light or weather; behind a hero with one line of type.
components.avoid_when: As generic "AI gradient" decoration; behind body text; on pages that already use WebGL.
components.reduced_motion: A designed still: a marbled sheet. Combed bands of the same three colours, like marbled paper keeping the trace of moving ink; no canvas is mounted.
components.touch: Runs at half resolution on coarse pointers.
components.a11y: Decorative canvas (aria-hidden); paused off screen and in hidden tabs; falls back to a CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable, loses its context, or renders wrong colours (it reads back one pixel to check). Keep all three colours dark (or all light) so text on top keeps its contrast everywhere.

components.name: Mesh Gradient
components.what: Four soft pools of colour drift very slowly over a ground colour and blend where they meet, like a dyed silk or a weather map. CSS only: each pool is a radial gradient moved with transform; no blur filter, no WebGL.
components.use_when: The palette itself is the brand (a paint, a cosmetics line, a dye house, a weather service), and a calmer, cheaper option than Liquid Field is right.
components.avoid_when: As the default "modern" hero background; behind body copy; with more than one other effect on the page; with clashing colours (the overlaps make new ones).
components.reduced_motion: A designed still: a colour study. The four colours laid out as soft horizontal fields (horizon, body, ground) with a fine grain; not the drift stopped.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). Capability probe (Save-Data, ≤ 2 cores, < 4 GB → still poster); transform-only Web Animations, paused off screen and in hidden tabs; absolute box, so no layout shift. Pick pool colours with the same lightness as the ground so text contrast holds everywhere. No canvas, so no DPR cost.

components.name: Meteors
components.what: Now and then a thin streak of light crosses a night sky at one shared angle and burns out; long quiet gaps between them. CSS only: each streak is a gradient line moved with transform.
components.use_when: Night skies, observatories, wishes, launches that are literal (a rocket club), New Year: behind one dark hero.
components.avoid_when: As "speed" or "innovation" decoration; light themes; more than one sky per page; busy sections where a flicker at the edge distracts from reading.
components.reduced_motion: A designed still: a long-exposure night, star trails wheeling round the pole and one bright meteor crossing them at the same angle, over a low horizon. The streak tracks are not rendered.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). Capability probe (Save-Data, ≤ 2 cores, < 4 GB → still poster). Streaks are short and sparse (one at a time on average, ≥ 4s gaps), so nothing flashes. Transform/opacity only via Web Animations that pause off screen and in hidden tabs; absolute box, so no layout shift. No canvas, so no DPR cost.

components.name: Particle Field
components.what: Dust drifting through a beam of light: soft particles at three depths, the near ones larger and brighter, all moving slowly sideways and bobbing. WebGL points; a CSS poster of scattered motes stands in elsewhere.
components.use_when: Cinema, projection, workshops, old rooms, archives, snowfall or pollen: a quiet atmosphere behind a dark hero.
components.avoid_when: "Tech" or "data" decoration; as a starfield warp; behind text-heavy sections; on pages that already run WebGL. For a cursor-reactive grid use Dot Field.
components.reduced_motion: A designed still: a star chart. The motes keep their density and depth, and a few are joined into constellations; no canvas is mounted.
components.touch: 60% of the particles at two-thirds resolution.
components.a11y: Decorative (aria-hidden). Capability probe (Save-Data, ≤ 2 cores, < 4 GB, no or software WebGL → poster); DPR ≤ 1.5; paused off screen and in hidden tabs; fills its absolute box, so no layout shift. Particles stay faint (alpha ≤ 0.9 on the nearest), so text contrast is checked against the ground.

components.name: Bento Reveal
components.what: A modular grid of mixed-size tiles that enter in reading order with a short stagger the first time the grid scrolls in.
components.use_when: Content that truly has mixed weights (one big feature, several small facts).
components.avoid_when: Equal-weight content (use a list); as the default landing layout (it's overused); more than one per page.
components.reduced_motion: Tiles are visible from the start.
components.a11y: A normal list; order in the DOM matches visual order.

components.name: Curve Carousel
components.what: Cards sit on a shallow arc; the focused card is upright and in front, its neighbours tilt and recede. Arrow keys, buttons, drag and swipe move it.
components.use_when: 3–9 case studies or products where one at a time is the point.
components.avoid_when: Content people need to compare; more than 9 items; as autoplaying decoration.
components.reduced_motion: Cards change position without easing.
components.a11y: A labelled region with previous/next buttons, aria-live status ("2 of 5"), and arrow-key support; hidden cards are inert.

components.name: Dock
components.what: A row of icon buttons that magnify smoothly as the cursor passes along them, neighbours growing a little less.
components.use_when: App-like tool collections, launchers and playful personal sites with 4–8 actions.
components.avoid_when: Primary navigation that needs labels; touch-first sites; more than 8 items.
components.reduced_motion: No magnification.
components.a11y: Real buttons or links with visible tooltips on focus and hover, and accessible names.

components.name: Flowing Menu
components.what: A big typographic list of links; hovering an item rolls a band over it from the edge the cursor entered, carrying a marquee of the item's words.
components.use_when: Portfolio and studio navigation or project indexes with 3–8 entries.
components.avoid_when: Primary site navigation on product sites; long lists; touch-first audiences.
components.reduced_motion: Hover shows the band instantly with still text.
components.touch: Plain links with a pressed state.
components.a11y: A nav with a normal list of links; the band and marquee are aria-hidden. Keyboard focus rolls the band in, so focus is as visible as hover (the row clips an outline).

components.name: Infinite Canvas
components.what: Drag (or use arrow keys) to pan an endless wall of tiles that repeats in every direction, with a little momentum when you let go.
components.use_when: The Gallery Wall archetype: archives, pin boards, studios with lots of visual work.
components.avoid_when: Fewer than ~12 tiles; content that needs order; as the only way to reach the work (also provide a list).
components.reduced_motion: No momentum; panning still works.
components.touch: One-finger drag pans; the page doesn't scroll while dragging inside.
components.a11y: A focusable region with arrow-key panning and an instruction label; provide a plain list of the same work elsewhere on the page.

components.name: Sticky Index
components.what: A sticky side index lists the page's sections and highlights the one you are reading, with a marker that slides between entries.
components.use_when: Long case studies, reports, documentation, annual reviews.
components.avoid_when: Short pages; mobile (it collapses to a top select); landing pages.
components.reduced_motion: The marker jumps instead of sliding.
components.touch: Hidden below 900px; sections stay in normal flow.
components.a11y: A nav of in-page links with aria-current on the active section.

components.name: Animated List
components.what: Entries arrive one at a time, like orders coming into a kitchen or messages into a log: each slides up into its slot and settles. It plays once, then the list is simply a list.
components.use_when: The content really arrives over time (orders, sign-ups, sensor readings, a changelog), and showing the arrival explains the product.
components.avoid_when: Fake "live activity" or social proof; long lists (over about 8 entries); content the visitor needs to scan at once.
components.reduced_motion: Every entry is there from the start.
components.touch: Same as desktop (plays when in view).
components.a11y: All entries are in the DOM from the first render (the hidden ones are opacity 0, which screen readers still read), so nothing is announced late and nothing is missed; slots are laid out from the start, so the list never pushes the page (no layout shift). It pauses off screen.

components.name: Confetti
components.what: Paper pieces burst from a point, tumble and flutter down under gravity and air drag, and are gone in under two seconds. Fired by you, from code, at a real moment.
components.use_when: A genuine, rare success the visitor caused: an order placed, a donation made, a course finished, a wedding RSVP. Once.
components.avoid_when: Page load; every button; form validation; serious contexts (payments for bills, health, legal); repeated triggers. For small click feedback use Click Spark.
components.reduced_motion: No particles at all; your success message carries the moment.
components.touch: Same as desktop (fire it from the tap's coordinates).
components.a11y: Purely decorative: a temporary, aria-hidden, pointer-events-none canvas that is removed after the burst. Pair it with a visible text confirmation. DPR ≤ 1.5; at most 120 pieces; runs only while pieces are on screen.

components.name: Device Mockup
components.what: A phone, browser or laptop frame drawn in CSS around real content (a screenshot or live markup). For a tall screenshot, pointing at the screen scrolls it slowly to the bottom, like someone reading.
components.use_when: Showing the actual product screen (an app, a site you built) where the device tells the visitor where it runs.
components.avoid_when: Stock "phone with a gradient" decoration; floating several devices at angles; screens with fake data; when the screen alone, unframed, reads better.
components.reduced_motion: A tall screen shows its whole page, still; any other screen can be scrolled with the wheel or keyboard.
components.touch: A tall screen shows its whole page (there is no hover to glide it); any other screen is a normal scroll area (swipe inside it).
components.a11y: The frame is decoration; the screen is a labelled region, focusable (tabindex 0) whenever it scrolls, so keyboard users can scroll it; a tall screen without the hover glide (touch, reduced motion) shows its whole page. The hover glide scrolls the screen (so the wheel, keyboard and zoom still reach every line), stops when the visitor scrolls it themselves, and returns when the pointer leaves. Sizes come from aspect-ratio, so no layout shift.

components.name: Glare Card
components.what: A flat, laminated card with a foil sheen: a soft band of colour and a sharp white glint slide across it as the pointer moves, the way a hologram on an ID card or a trading card catches light. The card itself never tilts (for tilt, use Tilt Card).
components.use_when: Passes, tickets, membership cards, collectibles, certificates: one small card that is a physical object.
components.avoid_when: Large surfaces (the blend is paint-heavy: its cost grows with area); photos of people; grids of many cards; anything that must look sober.
components.reduced_motion: A still, faint sheen at one angle; no glint movement.
components.touch: Dragging a finger moves the sheen; it rests at an angle otherwise.
components.a11y: The sheen layers are aria-hidden and sit above the artwork at low opacity, never over text that needs full contrast (keep text in the card's lower band or check contrast with the sheen at its brightest). Paint-heavy (blend mode), so it only updates while the pointer moves and is limited to the card (motion/tokens.md "What to animate").

components.name: Glow Border
components.what: The edge of a card lights up nearest the pointer, as if the pointer were a lamp held close to it; the light fades along the edge with distance. Only the border glows, never the surface.
components.use_when: A row or grid of dark cards or inputs where the pointer's position should feel physical (a control panel, a studio's service list, pricing tiers).
components.avoid_when: Light themes with low-contrast borders; single cards (no neighbours to compare); a page already using Spotlight Card on the same cards.
components.reduced_motion: A steady, faint border.
components.touch: A steady, faint border; the light follows a dragging finger.
components.a11y: The glow layer is aria-hidden behind a solid inner surface, so content contrast never changes. It moves with transform under a 1-border-wide gap (no animated mask or gradient position). The listener only runs while the card is on screen.

components.name: Icon Cloud
components.what: Labels or small icons sit on the surface of an invisible ball that turns slowly; dragging spins it and it coasts to a stop. The near side is large and sharp, the far side small and faint.
components.use_when: A collection the visitor browses for the pleasure of it (a herbarium's species, a type foundry's glyphs, a band's setlist history), with the full list available in text.
components.avoid_when: A logo wall of "technologies we use"; as navigation; more than about 40 items; small screens where a plain list reads better (below 300px wide it falls back to a wrapped list).
components.reduced_motion: The ball, still, at a fixed angle; dragging still turns it (the visitor's own motion).
components.touch: Drag sideways to spin; vertical swipes scroll the page.
components.a11y: The items are a real list in reading order; the 3D placement is visual only. It turns with transform (one rAF loop), pauses off screen and in hidden tabs, and stops auto-turning while the pointer is over it.

components.name: Loader Skeleton
components.what: Grey placeholder shapes in the exact layout of the content that's coming (an avatar, a title, a few lines), with a faint light passing over them, so the page doesn't jump when the content lands.
components.use_when: Content whose layout you know is loading (a card, a list row, a profile, an article), for waits over about 300ms.
components.avoid_when: Waits you can't predict the shape of (use Loader Spinner); placeholders that don't match the real layout (they cause the jump they're meant to prevent); whole pages of skeletons.
components.reduced_motion: The same shapes, with no passing light.
components.a11y: The wrapper is aria-busy with a visually hidden "Loading" label; the shapes are aria-hidden. Size the skeleton like the real content so swapping it causes no layout shift. The light pass is a transform-only overlay, paused off screen.

components.name: Loader Spinner
components.what: A thin ring whose arc stretches and shortens as it turns, for waits of unknown length. It only appears after a short delay, so fast loads never flash a spinner.
components.use_when: A wait you can't measure (a search, a payment check) inside a button, a panel or a page area.
components.avoid_when: Waits you can measure (show progress instead); content loading where the layout is known (use Loader Skeleton); whole-page splash screens.
components.reduced_motion: The ring holds still at three-quarters and the label is shown; nothing turns.
components.a11y: role="status" with a text label ("Loading" by default), visually hidden unless showLabel; appears after `delay` ms (default 300). The ring turns with transform; the arc length change is a small SVG stroke repaint, cheap at this size.

components.name: Orbiting Circles
components.what: Small badges travel on one or two thin circular orbits around a centre, staying upright as they go; the outer ring turns the other way, more slowly. Pointing at it stops the orbits.
components.use_when: A real centre with real satellites: a cooperative and its member farms, a studio and its long-term clients, a hub airport and its routes.
components.avoid_when: The generic "integrations around our logo" picture; more than about 10 satellites; anything the visitor must read while it moves (list them in text too).
components.reduced_motion: The same arrangement, still.
components.a11y: The centre and satellites are a labelled list for assistive tech (role="list"); the orbit art is presentational. Transform-only Web Animations that pause off screen, in hidden tabs, and on hover or focus.

components.name: Rainbow Border
components.what: A thin border made of a turning colour wheel around a card or button. It turns while you point at or focus the element and rests otherwise.
components.use_when: One element that is literally about colour (a paint, a print shop, a palette tool, a pride event), or the single "new" item in a list.
components.avoid_when: As generic "AI glow"; on more than one element per screen; serious or quiet brands; around body text blocks.
components.reduced_motion: The same colour border, still.
components.a11y: Decorative: the border layer is aria-hidden and the content sits on its own solid surface, so text contrast never depends on the colours. Turning uses transform: rotate on an oversized layer clipped by the frame (no animated gradient angle, which would repaint every frame). Pauses off screen.

components.name: Shimmer Button
components.what: A button that a narrow band of light crosses once when you point at it or focus it, and that presses down slightly when clicked.
components.use_when: The one primary action on a dark or metallic surface (book, reserve, buy) where a little glint suits the material.
components.avoid_when: More than one per screen; secondary actions; a page already using Light Sweep; light, paper-like brands (the glint reads as plastic).
components.reduced_motion: No band; the press still darkens the button (colour, not movement).
components.touch: The band crosses on press; no hover needed.
components.a11y: A real <button> (or <a> with href). Focus ring is the browser's own, never removed. The band moves with transform only and runs once per trigger. Press feedback 120ms (UI feedback ≤ 250ms).

components.name: Spotlight Card
components.what: A dark card with a soft pool of light that follows the pointer across its surface, like a torch on a wall.
components.use_when: Night, theatre, cinema, exhibition or archive concepts: a grid of a few dark cards the visitor explores.
components.avoid_when: Light surfaces (the pool vanishes); a grid where every card already moves; content that must be read evenly lit.
components.reduced_motion: A fixed, soft pool near the top of the card.
components.touch: The pool rests near the top; dragging a finger moves it.
components.a11y: The light is a decorative, aria-hidden layer below the content, and the text contrast is checked against the unlit surface, so it reads with the light anywhere. The pool moves with transform (no repainted gradient).

components.name: Terminal
components.what: A terminal window replays a short session when it scrolls into view: each command types itself after the prompt, its output appears at once, then the next command starts.
components.use_when: The product really is used from a command line (a CLI, a dev tool, an install step), and the session shown is real and copy-pasteable.
components.avoid_when: As "techy" decoration for a product with no CLI; sessions longer than about 8 lines; fake output.
components.reduced_motion: The whole session is shown at once.
components.touch: Same as desktop (plays when in view).
components.a11y: The full session is in the DOM from the first render (hidden lines are opacity 0, which screen readers still read) inside a <pre> with an accessible label, and every line holds its final slot (no layout shift). Commands can be copied from the first frame. Plays once.

components.name: Brand Selection
components.what: Text selection uses the brand accent and ink instead of the browser's blue, scoped to a section or the whole page.
components.use_when: Almost always; it's a tiny, free detail that shows care.
components.avoid_when: The accent and its text colour don't pass 4.5:1 together.
components.reduced_motion: Not applicable (no motion).
components.a11y: Check the contrast of selection text on the selection colour (scripts/contrast.mjs).

components.name: Click Spark
components.what: A tiny burst of lines radiates from the click point inside a wrapped area, then disappears.
components.use_when: Playful brands, games, and one celebratory action (a like, a ticket added).
components.avoid_when: Every click on the page; serious briefs; forms.
components.reduced_motion: No spark.
components.a11y: Decorative SVG lines (aria-hidden, pointer-events none); children keep their roles.

components.name: Copy Confirm
components.what: A copy button whose icon morphs to a tick and whose label says "Copied" for two seconds, then returns.
components.use_when: Install commands, email addresses, codes and coupon strings.
components.avoid_when: Content the user should read rather than paste.
components.reduced_motion: The tick swaps in without the morph.
components.a11y: A real button; aria-live announces "Copied"; falls back to selecting the text when the clipboard API is unavailable.

components.name: Count Up
components.what: A number counts from a start value to its real value once, when it first enters the screen, with tabular figures so it doesn't jitter.
components.use_when: Real, sourced figures that are the point of a section (one to three per page).
components.avoid_when: Invented or rounded-up stats; prices; anything a screenshot mid-count would misreport (see the v2 benchmark note).
components.reduced_motion: Shows the final value at once.
components.a11y: The final value is in the accessible name from the start; the counting digits are aria-hidden. Before it counts, the visible value is the final value (no-JS and screenshots never show 0).

components.name: Hold to Commit
components.what: An important action fills while you press and hold, and only confirms when the fill completes; letting go early drains it back.
components.use_when: Irreversible or weighty actions: delete, publish, donate, sign.
components.avoid_when: Everyday actions; anything time-critical; as the only way to confirm (keyboard users get Enter-to-hold too).
components.reduced_motion: The fill still shows progress (it's information) but with a linear, unanimated drain.
components.touch: Press and hold works with touch; long-press callouts are suppressed.
components.a11y: A real button; Space or Enter held works like a press; the label says "Hold to …"; aria-live announces completion. A click that was not a hold (screen readers, voice control and switch access synthesize these) arms a confirmation instead: the label becomes "Press again to confirm", it is announced, and a second activation within 6 s commits; double-clicks don't count. Pending frames are cancelled on unmount, and a hold stops if the window loses focus or the tab is hidden.

components.name: Remembered List
components.what: A list of links quietly marks the ones you've already opened (a small tick and a lighter weight), remembered across visits on this device.
components.use_when: Project lists, article archives, course modules, menus people browse more than once.
components.avoid_when: Lists that change identity often; sensitive topics where "visited" is private information on shared devices.
components.reduced_motion: The mark appears without a transition.
components.a11y: Visited items get a visually hidden "(opened)" suffix; storage is local only and fails silently.

components.name: Squish Switch
components.what: A toggle whose knob stretches while pressed and squashes as it lands on the other side, like a soft rubber key.
components.use_when: Light-hearted products and settings panels where a little character is welcome.
components.avoid_when: Serious financial or medical settings; dense settings tables.
components.reduced_motion: The knob moves without stretching.
components.a11y: A real button with role switch and aria-checked; the label is visible text.

components.name: Sticker Scatter
components.what: Clicking the logo or name bursts a handful of on-brand stickers (emoji or short glyphs) that fly out, spin, land and fade, like emptying a pocket of stickers.
components.use_when: Light-hearted personal sites, festivals, kids' brands and events; the logo only.
components.avoid_when: Serious or institutional briefs; buttons that do something else; repeated clicks on every page element.
components.reduced_motion: Stickers appear around the logo and fade without flying or spinning.
components.a11y: The trigger keeps its normal role and name; stickers are aria-hidden and never block clicks.

styles.name: Minimal
styles.keywords: quiet clean space restraint luxury architecture
styles.type_hint: one display + one text; weight contrast
styles.body:
# Style: Minimal

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** fewer things, each perfect. Space and type do the work.
**Use when:** the product or work is strong enough to stand alone: architecture, luxury, design studios, quiet portfolios.
**Avoid when:** the audience needs dense information quickly (dashboards, marketplaces).

- **Type:** one display face at a large scale, one text face. Weight contrast instead of colour contrast.
- **Colour:** warm or cool neutrals plus one accent at ≤ 3% of the screen.
- **Layout:** large margins, asymmetric placement, one focal point per screen, hairline rules for structure.
- **Motion:** Tier 1–2. Line reveals, slow image fades, precise hover states. Motion is felt, not watched.
- **Signature ideas:** Line Curtain, Proximity Weight on one word, Remembered List.
- **Pitfall:** minimal ≠ empty. Every empty area must frame something. If the page feels unfinished, add precision (captions, numbers, alignment), not decoration.

**Award-site teardowns** (principles, no code): `references/teardowns/lusion-v3.md`

styles.name: Editorial
styles.body:
# Style: Editorial

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** the web as a great magazine: masthead, columns, captions, pull quotes and confident headlines.
**Use when:** there's a story or a lot of content: studios, publications, culture, long-form product stories.
**Avoid when:** the page is a single action (a sign-up form).

- **Type:** a high-contrast serif or sharp grotesk for headlines, a book serif or neutral sans for text, mono for metadata.
- **Colour:** paper and ink, with an accent borrowed from print (vermilion, ultramarine, a press green).
- **Layout:** multi-column grids, margin notes, folios, drop caps used once, full-bleed photo spreads.
- **Motion:** Tier 2. Line reveals, ink fills, Stacked Deck for features, cross-document page transitions (Tier 3).
- **Signature ideas:** Ink Fill manifesto, Broadsheet archetype, Darkroom Develop images.
- **Pitfall:** fake magazine clichés (random "Issue No. 07" labels). Use editorial devices only where they organise real content.

**Award-site teardowns** (principles, no code): `references/teardowns/scout-motors.md`

styles.name: Swiss
styles.body:
# Style: Swiss / International

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** objective, grid-true, typographic clarity. Strong asymmetry, flush-left, rag-right.
**Use when:** precision is the brand: engineering, architecture, cultural institutions, systems products.
**Avoid when:** the brand's warmth or play matters more than clarity.

- **Type:** a neo-grotesk with character (Switzer, Neue Montreal, Schibsted Grotesk), with sizes on a strict modular scale.
- **Colour:** white or off-white, black, and one pure signal (red, orange, blue).
- **Layout:** a visible modular grid, numbers as structure, large type aligned to grid lines, flush-left everything.
- **Motion:** Tier 1–2. Elements slide along grid lines only (x or y, never diagonals), with hard ease-out.
- **Signature ideas:** a grid that draws itself on load, index numbers that count to their value, Ledger archetype.
- **Pitfall:** copying 1960s poster clichés (rotated type at 45° for no reason).

**Award-site teardowns** (principles, no code): `references/teardowns/terminal-industries.md`

styles.name: Neobrutalism
styles.body:
# Style: Neobrutalism

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** honest, raw and loud: hard borders, flat colour, visible structure, a sense of humour.
**Use when:** youth brands, creative tools, indie products, events, anything that wants to be disarming.
**Avoid when:** luxury, healthcare, finance trust contexts.

- **Type:** a heavy grotesk or a quirky display (Bricolage Grotesque, Cabinet Grotesk, Unbounded). A mono for labels.
- **Colour:** 2–3 flat saturated colours with black ink; offset solid shadows (`4px 4px 0 #000`).
- **Layout:** thick 2–3px borders, stacked blocks, deliberate misalignment, sticker-like badges.
- **Motion:** Tier 1–2. Snappy (120–200ms), offset-shadow presses (the element moves into its shadow), no soft easing.
- **Signature ideas:** Sticker Scatter, a press that "stamps", a marquee with velocity skew.
- **Pitfall:** ugly ≠ brutalist. Spacing, alignment and hierarchy still have to be immaculate.

styles.name: Glass
styles.body:
# Style: Glass

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** translucent layers over a rich background, depth through blur and light.
**Use when:** the concept is about layers, light or transparency (a weather app, a lens, a translucent product, an OS-like interface).
**Avoid when:** you only want it because it looks "modern". Glass without a reason is the most common AI tell.

- **Type:** a clean grotesk with good small-size legibility. Text sits on solid enough tint to keep contrast.
- **Colour:** a real image or a meaningful gradient behind the glass; glass tint 8–20% with `backdrop-filter: blur(16–28px) saturate(140%)`.
- **Layout:** few panels, clear depth order, a 1px inner highlight border.
- **Motion:** Tier 2–3. Panels move in parallax relative to the background; light sweeps across on hover.
- **Signature ideas:** a lens (Cursor Signatures #2) that sharpens the blurred layer, a glass panel that follows the scroll like a viewfinder.
- **Pitfall:** contrast failure on busy backgrounds. Test every text-on-glass pair at the worst point of the background.

**Award-site teardowns** (principles, no code): `references/teardowns/igloo-inc.md`

styles.name: Soft
styles.body:
# Style: Soft / Neumorphism

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** soft extruded surfaces lit from one side, tactile and calm.
**Use when:** small, tactile interfaces (controls, a device companion app, a wellness product).
**Avoid when:** content-heavy pages; the low contrast hurts reading and accessibility.

- **Type:** a rounded or soft grotesk (General Sans, Satoshi). Larger text sizes to compensate for low-contrast surfaces.
- **Colour:** one mid-light base with paired light and dark shadows, plus one accent for state.
- **Layout:** controls as objects; generous radius (16–28px).
- **Motion:** Tier 1–2. Press = shadow inverts (inset); spring-like but short (200–300ms).
- **Signature ideas:** Hold to Commit on a soft button, a dial that rotates with scroll.
- **Pitfall:** invisible boundaries. Add a subtle 1px border or stronger shadow for 3:1 non-text contrast.

styles.name: Flat / Illustrative
styles.body:
# Style: Flat / Illustrative

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** solid colour, clear shapes, friendly illustration, no depth effects.
**Use when:** education, public services, children's products, explainer-heavy products.
**Avoid when:** luxury or very technical audiences.

- **Type:** a friendly grotesk with open apertures (Onest, Hanken Grotesk, Instrument Sans).
- **Colour:** a limited palette of 3–5 flat colours with strong contrast pairs.
- **Layout:** illustration-led sections, clear steps, big tap targets.
- **Motion:** Tier 1–3. Lottie or Rive illustrations that explain, SVG line drawing (Thread).
- **Signature ideas:** a mascot or shape built in Rive that reacts to form states.
- **Pitfall:** stock "corporate blob people" illustrations. Commission or build a specific visual system.

styles.name: Kinetic Type
styles.keywords: moving words variable axes split letters
styles.body:
# Style: Kinetic Type

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** typography is the image and the motion. Words move, stretch, split and react.
**Use when:** portfolios, music, events, launches, type foundries, any brand with a strong voice.
**Avoid when:** long reading content (keep body text still).

- **Type:** variable fonts with expressive axes (width, weight, optical size, custom axes). See `data/fonts.csv` for faces with axes.
- **Colour:** monochrome so the motion reads, with one accent for emphasis.
- **Layout:** type at 15–40vw, edge to edge, overlapping layers of words.
- **Motion:** Tier 2–5. SplitText choreography, variable-axis animation, scroll-velocity width, scrubbed type films.
- **Signature ideas:** Proximity Weight, Width Sprint, Letter Relay, Neighbour Moves.
- **Pitfall:** readability. Each word must be readable when still, and every mid-animation frame must be readable within 300ms.

**Award-site teardowns** (principles, no code): `references/teardowns/lando-norris.md`

styles.name: Organic
styles.body:
# Style: Organic / Natural

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** warmth, texture and imperfection: paper grain, soft curves, natural colour.
**Use when:** food, craft, wellness, sustainability, hospitality.
**Avoid when:** the brand is about speed or precision.

- **Type:** a serif with soft details (Fraunces with SOFT axis, Young Serif, Gambetta) and a humanist sans for text.
- **Colour:** earth and plant tones sampled from real photos. No neon.
- **Layout:** asymmetric, image-led, occasional hand-drawn marks or torn edges used with restraint.
- **Motion:** Tier 2. Slow (800–1200ms) drifts, Darkroom Develop, gentle parallax on texture layers.
- **Signature ideas:** text that "grows" (line reveal with a slight rotation settle), a seed-to-plant scroll film.
- **Pitfall:** rustic clichés (wood textures, script fonts everywhere).

styles.name: Dark Luxe
styles.body:
# Style: Dark Luxe

> **Standards vs style:** this style may override house-style defaults (canvas, type scale, grid, accent); it never overrides the universal standards in `principles/restraint.md`.

**Essence:** a dark room, one light source, precious details.
**Use when:** premium products, hotels, fragrance, watches, automotive, night-life.
**Avoid when:** accessibility-critical public information, or bright, friendly brands.

- **Type:** a refined high-contrast serif (Bodoni Moda, Gloock, Zodiak) or a wide elegant sans, set with generous tracking at small sizes.
- **Colour:** near-black grounds (#0B0B0C–#151412), warm off-white ink, metallic accents (brass, champagne) used tiny.
- **Layout:** centred compositions are allowed here as a ritual, with lots of black space.
- **Motion:** Tier 2–5. Light sweeps, slow push-ins, product turntables via image sequence (Motomation).
- **Signature ideas:** a Motomation product film, Aperture transitions, a cursor torch that lights the scene.
- **Pitfall:** grey-on-black contrast failures and "gold gradient" clichés.

**Award-site teardowns** (principles, no code): `references/teardowns/siena-film-foundation.md` · `references/teardowns/cartier-watches-wonders-2025.md`

about.title: What it is
about.body: Motomation Design is a set of instructions, data files and small scripts that a coding AI (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and similar tools) reads before it designs a website. Without it, an AI asked for a website usually produces the same page every time: a centred headline, two buttons, three feature boxes, a purple gradient. With it, the AI is made to work out what this particular brief is about first, pick a page structure on purpose, choose fonts and colours from a curated list with a stated reason, keep animation to what the page needs, and then measure the finished page in a real browser before it hands it over. It is a working method, not a template pack: the output is written for each brief.

about.title: Who it is for
about.body: - **People who build websites with an AI coding tool** and are tired of every result looking alike: freelancers, small studios, founders, developers without a designer.

about.title: The problem it solves
about.body: Most design skills for AI agents are one of two things: a list of rules ("don't use purple gradients"), or a box of parts (components to paste in). Rules alone don't produce ideas, and parts alone produce pages that look like the parts. Motomation does three things those don't:

about.title: The philosophy in one paragraph
about.body: A good website has one idea and says it well. Type is chosen first and with a reason; on a portfolio or brand site it can be the main image, on a dashboard it leads by being clear rather than big. Motion is allowed only when it tells the visitor something, and there is always a designed version for people who turn motion off. Everything that doesn't serve the idea is removed: one signature move, not five. Accessibility, real content and performance are standards, not style, so no brief can switch them off.

about.title: A typical session, start to finish
about.body: 1. **You install it** in your project with one command (`npx skills add asfakulsiam/asfakulsiam-motomation-design`) and give your agent a brief, for example: "/build a site for a 12-room hotel in Sylhet that sells quiet."

about.title: What it does not do
about.body: - **It doesn't guarantee originality across the internet.** The memory only knows about your project. Two people with the same brief and seed can get similar plans.

headline.against: Tier 4 motion, motion only from gate.mjs --report strips (9)

findings: The gate is about half the win. A baseline that only runs `gate.mjs` has no hard-gate failures (0 of 15, against 6 for the plain baseline) but isn't better designed (raw 73.0 → 68.3 against the plain baseline), and the skill still beats it 14–1.

Effort explains part of v2's 15–0. A baseline told to work about as long as the skill beats the plain baseline 12–0–3 and takes 5 of 15 pairs from the skill, including all three ceramics-shop seeds. 10–5 is not significant with 15 pairs (sign test p≈0.30).

On motion alone the skill lost. At Tier 4, judged only from the gate's scroll-frame strips, the baseline won 6 of 9 seeds. The weakest axis was the reduced-motion fallback (2.50 vs 4.39 of 5). Every skill page reached for WebGL.
In Codex the gate often couldn't run (the headless browser crashed or timed out in a loaded sandbox). 3 of 5 skill runs shipped without a verified pass, and the SaaS page broke.
One skill page failed a hard gate (ceramics s3103: dimmed scroll-sequence steps at 2.1:1 that `gate.mjs` measured only in their active state).

findings: Draws (Part A): 5 seeds gave 5 archetypes, 4 signatures and 4 mutations. 1 of 10 pairs is at or above 0.70: seeds 3101 and 3104 share the `rows` layout family and a scroll signature, and their tiers differ by 3. Mean similarity is 0.28.

Builds (Part B): the 15 published skill builds use 12 different archetypes across 15 runs (timeline and room appear in both hotel and studio). Within each brief, every signature is different. Within a brief, archetypes differ in 4 of 5 briefs. SaaS used `console` twice (2101, 2102), so SaaS fails the release gate's variety rule ("3 runs, 3 different archetypes and signatures") on archetype. The other four briefs pass it.

Max 1.00 in four briefs is a limit of the fingerprint, not identical pages. A build's stamp gives only archetype, signature and tier. The builds' signatures are invented for each brief, not rows of `signatures.csv`, so their type is unknown. Every v2 build chose Tier 2. That leaves two dimensions, layout family and tier, so two different archetypes in the same family (timeline and room are both `sequence`) score 1.00. Measuring section order and type scale from the built HTML would make Part B sharper. That isn't done here.

Not done: 5 real builds of one brief. That needs an agent run, and none was available in this environment (see `../README.md`, "Agents tested so far"). Part B uses the 3 builds per brief that already exist.
